newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Howard tells Australians to accept Malaysian laws.
newsitem.headline: Howard tells Australians to accept Malaysian laws.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard on Monday reacted to Malaysia's crackdown on a East Timor human rights conference by telling Australians they had to live and let live.
"Let me simply say that different countries do things differently," he told reporters. "We do things our way, other countries do things their way."

Malaysia on Monday deported 10 foreigners who participated in a banned political conference in Kuala Lumpur that was closed down by pro-government demonstrators on Saturday. Thirty-six others were deported on Sunday.

An Australian bishop was among the 46 foreigners detained at the conference. An Australian journalist covering the event for the Australian Broadcasting Corporation was also arrested and reported on Monday she had been held in "appalling" conditions.
"If we are to have sensible relations with the nations of the region we ought to understand what they are and also what they are not," Howard said.

"There is a tradition of free public assembly in Australia which is almost unique in the world. We are always going to be different on things like that, I think proudly different. But if we are to live in this region we have to all of us sort of understand that."
Australia, with old democratic traditions, has had a sometimes uneasy relationship with regional neighbours, but Canberra heavily promotes the need for the country to integrate itself with Asia.
"I don't see my role as the prime minister of this country to give endless moral lectures to the rest of the region," Howard said.
Differences between Australia and its neighbours have been emphasised since an independent member of parliament, Pauline Hanson, stirred up a debate on Asian immigration.
However, both sides of Australian politics have rejected Hanson's call for an immediate halt to immigration and her warning that Asians were swamping the country.
